items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian benchmark indices opened flat and remained under pressure throughout the session. Analysts suggest the Nifty's immediate bias remains down, targeting key support levels. The India VIX, a fear gauge, rose significantly, indicating market anxiety. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutional investors were net buyers on Monday. The Indian rupee traded in a narrow range due to RBI intervention and oil price concerns.

items.title: Indian firms line up $7.7 billion in ECB proposals in July
items.description: Indian companies filed proposals worth $7.70 billion for external commercial borrowings in July. This represented a significant 27% growth over the previous month's figures. The Reserve Bank of India had eased its borrowing framework earlier in February. Air India and Interglobe Aviation together filed proposals worth $780 million. These companies sought special permissions from the central bank for their borrowings.

items.title: Gold loans, consumer durables drive NBFC credit growth to 14.9% in July
items.description: Non-banking financial companies saw 14.9 percent credit expansion by July end. This growth accelerated from last year's 10.6 percent expansion. Gold loans surged 68.5 percent and consumer durable loans grew 51.5 percent. Retail loans within NBFCs increased 21.4 percent, showing strong performance. Housing and vehicle loans also recorded significant year-on-year growth.

items.title: Morgan Stanley’s top picks: Adani Power, Trent, among 10 stocks rated ‘overweight’ by Wall Street giant
items.description: Wall Street major Morgan Stanley in its latest strategy note suggests that India could be in the midst of a multi quarter growth upcycle. Given supportive equity valuations, we expect equity market performance to improve considerably in the coming months. It does not expect a bunching of issuances, with retail demand continuing to stay ahead of supply. Sensex earnings are expected to compound at 16% annually through F2029. Here are 10 stocks the brokerage is bullish on.

items.title: Defence exports rise after Operation Sindoor. Jefferies names Solar, Astra, HAL and BEL as top stock picks
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on Solar Industries and Astra Microwave with Buy ratings, citing strong defence growth prospects and rising order books. It also maintained Buy ratings on HAL and Bharat Electronics while assigning a Hold rating to Bharat Dynamics. The brokerage expects robust earnings growth across these companies, supported by rising defence spending, indigenisation and export opportunities.

items.title: LIC, HDFC Life, other stocks rise up to 3% as Aug new business premium jumps 33% YoY. What Nuvama, others are saying
items.description: Life insurers reported a 33% YoY increase in total new business premium to Rs 41,198 crore in August, led by a sharp rise in group single-premium business. LIC posted more than 45% growth, while SBI Life and HDFC Life saw stronger retail-weighted premium growth.

items.title: Sensex falls 300 points, Nifty below 23,700 as market extends losses. How long will the downtrend continue?
items.description: Indian stock markets opened lower on Tuesday, continuing their downward trajectory. The surge in crude oil prices coupled with anxieties over Federal Reserve rate hikes are major contributors to this decline. Moreover, the active IPO market is siphoning off significant capital from traditional stocks. Analysts expect this trend to extend in the near future and recommend that investors shift their focus toward large-cap stocks for improved risk-reward outcomes.

items.title: GE Vernova shares surge 8% as firm declared lowest bidder for Power Grid project; Nomura raises target price
items.description: GE Vernova T&D India shares rose after the company emerged as the lowest bidder for a 6,000 MW HVDC project from Power Grid. Nomura raised its target price to Rs 6,000, while Emkay retained its Buy rating with a Rs 5,300 target price. Both brokerages highlighted strong prospects in the transmission sector, capacity expansion, robust cash flows, and healthy earnings growth.

items.title: Coforge shares double from March low, outperform Nifty IT peers. Is more steam left in the rally?
items.description: Coforge shares have experienced a remarkable resurgence, doubling since March and leaving its IT competitors behind. The company recently announced impressive growth in net profit and revenue during the first quarter. Analysts anticipate that mid-tier IT firms like Coforge will thrive amid evolving industry dynamics. Both Jefferies and Axis Direct express optimism about Coforge's growth trajectory. The stock has consistently yielded positive returns over the last year.

items.title: CAS rewrites closing bell: How capital-market stocks performed in 1 month & what comes next
items.description: Following the introduction of the Closing Auction Session, capital-market stocks displayed a range of performances. While Motilal Oswal Financial Services and MCX enjoyed substantial gains exceeding 20 per cent, companies like Indian Energy Exchange, BSE, HDFC AMC, and CAMS experienced significant falls. The uptick in trading activity sparked gains for several brokerages and wealth management firms. Future market dynamics will largely hinge on trading volumes and clarity in regulations.

items.title: Syrma SGS Technology among 4 stocks showing White Marubozu Pattern
items.description: On September 7, four stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Supreme Industries among 4 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On September 7, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 2.5% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge. An uptrend signal occurs when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, indicating strengthening momentum in the stock's price. The RSI is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: HAL, Astra Microwave, other defence stocks rally up to 4% after DAC clears Rs 1.10L cr proposals; Motilal picks 3 stocks to buy
items.description: Defence stocks: The Defence Acquisition Council approved defence procurement proposals worth around Rs 1.10 lakh crore, with nearly 98% of purchases to be sourced from Indian companies. The move is likely to keep defence stocks such as HAL, BEL, Paras Defence, BEML and Astra Microwave in focus. The approvals cover requirements of the Army, Navy and Air Force.

items.title: FIIs poured nearly Rs 50,000 crore into these sectors in last 2 months. Here’s what they bought
items.description: Foreign investors turned net buyers in India, deploying Rs 49,830 crore across sectors in July and August, with consumer services, healthcare, consumer durables, financials and IT emerging as the biggest beneficiaries. The shift reflects stronger domestic growth, better-than-expected Q1 earnings and a stabilising rupee, while telecom, capital goods, power and select other sectors faced sustained selling.

items.title: Shiprocket shares gain 3% as Q1 net loss narrows to Rs 14 crore in first earnings post IPO; revenue up 34% YoY
items.description: Shiprocket reported a narrower consolidated net loss of Rs 13.7 crore in Q1FY27, compared with Rs 18 crore a year earlier, while revenue from operations rose 33.8% year-on-year to Rs 592.1 crore. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at Rs 8.9 crore, supported by strong growth in the emerging business, while core business revenue grew 22%.

items.title: Strong Start! Deepa Jewellers shares list at 25% premium over IPO price
items.description: Deepa Jewellers made an impressive debut on Dalal Street, launching with a 25% premium after its shares were priced at Rs 177 each. The public offering attracted overwhelming interest, evident by a staggering 42.61 times subscription. With plans to bolster working capital and inventory, Deepa Jewellers also reported a notable financial performance marked by rising income and profitability in FY26.

items.title: Rays of Belief shares make flat market debut, list at IPO price of Rs 239
items.description: Rays of Belief Ltd shares debuted flat at Rs 239 on September 8, matching the IPO price.  The Rs 125 crore IPO saw overwhelming subscription across all investor categories.  The company plans to use IPO proceeds for expanding learning infrastructure and technology upgrades.  Financials show strong revenue growth but a decline in profit after tax.  Rays of Belief offers intervention programs for children with neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Nifty slips below critical support level of 23,600 as market reacts to global economic uncertainties
items.description: Indian equity indices experienced a decline on Monday, with the Nifty 50 falling below 23,800. Rising Brent crude oil prices and investor preference for smaller stocks impacted large-cap performance. The market also faces pressure from increased IPOs and fund-raising activities. US bond yields are nearing their 2023 highs, causing investor discomfort. Mid and small-cap segments show stronger activity while large caps lag.

items.title: Life insurers' new business premium up 33% in August
items.description: Life insurers displayed impressive growth in new business premiums for August, with an overall year-on-year increase of thirty-three percent. This surge was predominantly driven by the single-premium and group business sectors, although retail-weighted premiums grew at a more moderate rate. Experts in the industry predict a return to more typical growth patterns in the following months.

items.title: MF Favourite Smallcaps: 14 stocks that soared up to 220% in CY26.
items.description: So far, CY26 has been a strong year for several small-cap stocks, with some delivering eye-catching returns in just over eight months. In fact, 28 Nifty Smallcap stocks have surged more than 50% so far this calendar year, including five multibaggers. We took the analysis a step further to identify stocks that are not only rallying but are also attracting meaningful institutional interest. We filtered for stocks held by more than five mutual fund schemes as of August 2026. When multiple mutual fund schemes hold the same stock, it can signal strong institutional conviction and broader professional investor interest, which may also help bolster retail investor confidence.After applying these filters, 14 stocks made the cut. Each has delivered a 50–220% rally in CY26, while three have emerged as multibaggers. The result is a focused list of smallcaps that combine strong price momentum with meaningful mutual fund participation, making them particularly interesting to track. (Data Source: ACE Equity, ACE MF)

items.title: PVR Inox’s Rs 300-crore buyback opens on Sept 10: Check buyback price, key dates, entitlement ratio
items.description: PVR Inox’s Rs 300-crore share buyback opens September 10 and closes September 17, offering eligible shareholders Rs 1,450 per share, over 25% above the market price. The company plans to repurchase nearly 21 lakh shares. Eligibility depends on the September 4 record date, with separate entitlement ratios for small and general shareholders.

items.title: Copper hits record high, UltraTech’s Ultravolt on the offensive: A double whammy for cable makers in FY27?
items.description: Copper prices have soared to unprecedented levels, creating ripple effects on manufacturing expenses worldwide. UltraTech's Ultravolt is making bold strides into the Indian wires and cables sector, creating a competitive landscape for established manufacturers in fiscal year 2027. As a response to escalating input costs, companies are enacting price hikes, raising investor apprehensions about increased competition and dwindling profit margins.

items.title: FCNR(B) windfall for banks explained: Who got highest inflows and what it means for investors
items.description: FCNR(B) deposits offer banks a cheaper and balance-sheet-efficient source of funding, but their finite tenor and initial deployment challenges could pressure margins. While ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank stand to benefit from higher inflows, IDFC First Bank offers the strongest earnings upside. Investors may see margin pressure initially before stronger liquidity, loan growth and lower funding costs support earnings.

items.title: PC Jeweller shares fall 5% after sharp 3-day rally; stock up 388% in 3 years
items.description: PC Jeweller shares retreated after a 37% three-session rally, likely due to profit booking. Despite the decline, the stock remains up 31% in a week and 45% in 2026, with gains of 388% over three years and 424% over five years.

items.title: HFCL, Sterlite Tech shares jump 5%: What’s driving up to 705% multibagger run?
items.description: HFCL and Sterlite Technologies hit their upper circuits on Tuesday, extending their sharp 2026 rallies on strong business updates. HFCL has surged over 267% so far this year, while Sterlite Tech has delivered a staggering 705% return, making both standout multibaggers.

items.title: Biocon shares rise 2% on 10-year Pertuzumab supply deal for breast cancer therapy in Brazil
items.description: Biocon shares rose after the company secured a 10-year Pertuzumab supply contract in Brazil. The consortium with Bahiafarma and Bionovis received full allocation under the country’s PDP programme, providing access to around 70% of public-sector demand.

items.title: Ashish Kacholia's portfolio: How ace investor's top 5 stock holdings performed in one month?
items.description: Ace investor Ashish Kacholia is closely tracked for his stock picks. Often called the 'Big Whale' of the Indian stock market, Kacholia publicly holds around 48 stocks worth nearly Rs 3,190 crore, according to Trendlyne data. Here are his top five holdings and their performance in the past one month.

items.title: Explosive Gains! ESDS Software shares skyrocket 195% from IPO price in 3 sessions
items.description: ESDS Software shares extended their post-listing rally for a third session, rising 16.21% to Rs 1,266, nearly 195% above the IPO price of Rs 429. The surge follows a 136-times subscribed IPO, improved financial performance and plans to invest heavily in cloud and data-centre infrastructure.

items.title: IFCI shares slide 7% after stellar 30% monthly surge amid NSE IPO buzz
items.description: IFCI shares fell 7% after a sharp recent rally, after the stock rallied nearly 30% in a month amid Sebi’s approval of the NSE IPO. IFCI has indirect exposure to NSE through its stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India.

items.title: SaaS is beating the ‘SaaSpocalypse’! CLSA explains what AI means for Indian IT stocks
items.description: CLSA sees AI widening the gap between SaaS platforms and Indian IT services, favouring Persistent Systems and LTIMindtree. SaaS firms are gaining productivity, while system integrators face automation pressure. Both companies are adapting through deal growth, AI adoption and higher-value engineering work.

items.title: Hindustan Copper shares jump 4% as copper prices surge to all-time high. What’s driving the red metal’s red hot rally?
items.description: Hindustan Copper shares jumped over 4% as copper prices hit record highs amid supply concerns and a weaker US dollar. LME copper touched $14,533 per tonne, while MCX futures neared lifetime highs. Hindustan Copper, India’s only integrated copper producer with captive mines, has gained over 115% in the past year.
